questions.question: Where on the carriageway should you normally position your car on a two-way road in Iceland?
options: In the exact middle of your own driving lane at all times
Slightly left of centre so you can see further ahead
As far left as possible to keep clear of the road edge
As far to the right as possible without obstructing cyclists or pedestrians
questions.explanation: Iceland has right-hand traffic, so keeping right is the default, and it matters most on rises, in blind bends and wherever visibility is short. Road users near the edge must still be given room.

questions.question: You need to drive noticeably slower than the surrounding traffic. What does the law require of you?
options: Switch on hazard lights and keep your normal lane position
Stay in the left lane so faster traffic can pass you on the right
Stop at the first junction and let the whole queue overtake
Keep well right and use a pullout on narrow roads to let others pass
questions.explanation: Obstructing traffic without good reason is prohibited. A slow driver must stay on the rightmost lane and actively help others get past, because unusually slow driving raises accident risk.

questions.question: What penalty can a driver expect for failing to give way to a pedestrian at a pedestrian crossing?
options: A written warning on the first offence only
A fine and four penalty points
A fine and two penalty points
Immediate suspension of the driving licence
questions.explanation: Giving way to pedestrians who intend to cross is unconditional, and the book states the sanction as a fine plus two penalty points on the driving record.

questions.question: When is an ambulance or police car allowed to depart from the general traffic rules?
options: Whenever the driver judges the trip to be urgent
Only when a second officer is travelling in the vehicle
At any time, since emergency services are always exempt
Only when responding with emergency lights and/or sirens switched on
questions.explanation: The exemption is tied to a signalled emergency run: the vehicle must be showing its emergency light system and/or sounding its siren, so other road users can recognise it.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle approaches from behind on a road with two lanes in your direction. What should you do?
options: Brake hard immediately wherever you happen to be
Signal right, move into the right lane and let it pass
Signal left and pull over onto the left-hand side
Speed up until you reach the next side road
questions.explanation: Emergency vehicles normally use the leftmost lane, so clearing that lane to the right is what helps. Sudden manoeuvres are to be avoided while doing it.

questions.question: At a junction with no traffic lights, stop sign or give way sign, who has priority?
options: The driver already travelling on the wider road
The driver approaching from your right
The driver approaching from your left
The driver who arrived at the junction first
questions.explanation: This is the right hand rule: you yield to traffic coming from your right and have priority over traffic from your left. Both drivers must still approach with care.

questions.question: In which situation does the right hand rule stop applying at a junction?
options: When the junction lies inside an urban area
When your road is wider than the crossing road
When lights, a stop sign or a give way sign controls it
When you are already travelling straight ahead
questions.explanation: Working traffic lights, stop signs and give way signs set the priority themselves and override the right hand rule, as does an officer directing traffic.

questions.question: Two cars meet while manoeuvring inside a car park. How is priority decided?
options: The right hand rule does not apply off the public road
The car that is reversing has priority
The car nearer the exit has priority
The right hand rule applies
questions.explanation: The right hand rule extends to open areas such as parking lots, so a driver crossing your path from the right must be let through.

questions.question: You reach a junction with a give way sign facing you. What must you do?
options: Give way only to traffic coming from your right
Stop completely at the line in every case
Give way to traffic from both the right and the left
Continue if you can cross without touching the other lane
questions.explanation: A give way sign removes your priority against all traffic on the crossing road, from either side. Slow down early and stop if the situation requires it.

questions.question: At a stop sign, when may a driver roll through the junction without halting?
options: When no other traffic is anywhere near the junction
Never, the car must always come to a complete stop
When visibility along the crossing road is clear and long
When the car is already moving very slowly
questions.explanation: A stop sign demands a full stop regardless of whether any other traffic is present, and the front wheels should stay behind the stop line.

questions.question: Traffic beyond a light-controlled junction is queued solid. What should you do on the green light?
options: Wait before the junction until you can clear it fully
Enter and stop inside the junction to hold your place
Enter slowly and edge forward with the queue
Enter and then reverse back if the queue does not move
questions.explanation: You should not enter a junction unless you can drive out of it again; stopping inside blocks the crossing traffic when their signal changes.

questions.question: As you approach a road junction, which direction should you check first?
options: To the left, because that traffic reaches you sooner
The rear mirror, before anything outside the car
Straight ahead, since that is where you are going
To the right, because that traffic has priority
questions.explanation: Vehicles coming from the left cross your path earlier than those from the right, so they are checked first. You then look repeatedly in both directions.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to be on the inside of a long vehicle that is turning the same way as you?
options: The trailer's rear end swings into the inner lane
Long vehicles are allowed to take priority in turns
The long vehicle must brake sharply mid-turn
Your own rear wheels are pushed towards the kerb
questions.explanation: Because of its length, the back of a trailer drifts across into the inner lane during a tight turn, so leave the long vehicle enough room.

questions.question: What should you do with your speed just before you change lanes?
options: Slow down noticeably so you can slot in behind traffic
Accelerate hard so the gap opens up in front of you
Adjust it to match the speed of the lane you are entering
Hold the exact speed you had before checking the mirrors
questions.explanation: Matching the target lane's speed first lets you cross the line steadily and without forcing other drivers to react. Lanes divided by a continuous line may not be crossed at all.

questions.question: You are turning right at a junction on a carriageway with several lanes in your direction. Which lane do you use?
options: The rightmost lane before the junction and after it
Any lane, provided you signal early enough
A middle lane, then move right after the turn
The rightmost lane before the junction only
questions.explanation: A right turn is set up from the rightmost lane and completed into the rightmost lane of the road being entered, which keeps the turn tight and predictable.

questions.question: Who has the right of way between a car already circulating in a roundabout and one about to enter?
options: The car already driving inside the roundabout
The entering car, so the roundabout does not fill up
Whichever car is larger or heavier
The entering car if it is signalling right
questions.explanation: Traffic circulating in the roundabout keeps priority over traffic entering it, and road markings may add further guidance at individual roundabouts.

questions.question: Which of these is required of a driver inside a roundabout?
options: Changing to the outer lane one exit in advance
Signalling right before leaving the roundabout
Signalling left throughout the whole time inside
Choosing the inner lane whenever traffic is heavy
questions.explanation: The right indicator when exiting is mandatory. Changing lanes inside a roundabout is prohibited, and the first exit is always taken from the rightmost lane.
